ai.title: Enable codesearch and runfilechangehooks in SDK
ai.summary: SDK client now implements code_search via @vscode/ripgrep and stubs run_file_change_hooks as no-op. New types PublishedToolName and PublishedClientToolName restrict overrideTools to published client tools. code_search enforces project directory boundaries and truncates output at 10000 chars.

eli5.text: When you ask an agent to look through your code for matching text, it now actually scans your project files using a fast search engine instead of doing nothing. The search stays inside your project folder, so it can't wander into parent directories you didn't intend, and if the results get extremely long, they're cut off at a fixed size so nothing overloads the conversation. If an agent tries to run file-change hooks (like commands that trigger when a file is edited), those now quietly report that the feature isn't available in this environment rather than silently failing. Only tools that are officially published can be swapped out, so custom or experimental tools can no longer override the core published ones.

ai.title: Fix PostHog exitCode tracking for terminal commands
ai.summary: Corrects `runTerminalCommand` to spread `value[0].value` instead of `value` when calling `trackEvent` for `TERMINAL_COMMAND_COMPLETED`. Ensures `exitCode` and related metrics are captured in PostHog analytics. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/terminal/run-command.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the system now correctly reports whether the command succeeded or failed to the analytics tool, instead of sending incomplete information. You wouldn't see this directly, but if someone looked at the usage data, they'd now see accurate pass/fail counts for terminal commands. This is a behind-the-scenes fix that improves the reliability of internal tracking metrics.

ai.title: Track credits and runtime in git evals
ai.summary: Git evals now record `totalCostUsd` and `runtime_sec` per run, aggregating them into `average_cost_usd` and `average_runtime_sec` overall metrics. `Runner['run']` returns `totalCostUsd`, derived from `chunk.total_cost_usd` in `ClaudeRunner` and `creditsUsed / 100` in `CodebuffRunner`. `EvalRunJudged` and `FullEvalLog` types updated in `evals/git-evals/types.ts`. `runSingleEval` accumulates costs from `codebuffResult.totalCostUsd` across prompts.

eli5.text: The software that automatically tests AI coding tools now tracks how much money each test costs and how long it takes to run. If you looked at a test report from this internal testing system, you'd see a new cost figure per test and two new averages, average cost and average runtime, alongside the existing scores. The testing tool records the cost when a test runs, adds it up across all the tests, and then includes both the total and the average in the final report it generates.

ai.title: Add cost breakdown to eval email
ai.summary: Added cost and runtime metrics to `formatEvalSummaryForEmail`. Computes average/total cost and runtime from `overall_metrics`. Includes detailed per-set cost breakdown and efficiency ratios in the email body.

eli5.text: The daily summary email that the internal team receives after running code evaluations now includes cost and timing information. You will notice new dollar amounts and seconds-per-run figures in the email subject line and body, showing how much each evaluation run cost, how long it took, and how much was spent overall. This update is live today for anyone who receives those evaluation result emails.

ai.title: Add cost info to git eval judge prompt
ai.summary: Added [COST_INFORMATION] block to judge-git-eval.ts prompt. Displays total cost in USD with two decimal places. Internal change affecting eval scoring context.

eli5.text: When someone reviews how well our assistant performs a task, they now see a note telling them exactly how much that review cost in dollars and cents. The reviewer (a person who judges the assistant's work) will spot a new line showing "Total Cost: $X.XX USD" alongside the timing info, so they understand the expense behind each evaluation. This is live today and only affects internal reviews, not anything an outside user would see.

ai.title: Add package.json to initial agents directory template
ai.summary: Added package.json to common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir. This file defines metadata for custom Codebuff agents, specifying name, version, description, and Apache-2.0 license. Ensures proper package context for agent files in new projects.

eli5.text: When a new project is created, it will now include a small configuration file in the custom assistants folder. This file tells the system that the folder holds your personalized AI assistants and describes what they do, along with the license terms. You would only notice this if you looked inside the assistants folder of a freshly created project; it does not change how the assistants themselves behave.

ai.title: Add Apache 2.0 license to initial agents template
ai.summary: Added `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/LICENSE` containing Apache License 2.0 text. Ensures agent templates distributed by Freebuff carry explicit licensing terms. Scope limited to shared core templates; no runtime logic or user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: When new agent projects are first created, they now include a copy of the standard Apache 2.0 license file, so anyone who gets or copies that starter project will see the licensing terms right away instead of wondering how they're allowed to use it. This only affects the initial project templates bundled with the software, it doesn't change how running agents behave or add any new functionality.
